Casey County, Kentucky, which takes its name from his great-grandfather, Colonel William Casey. His grandfather, Colonel Robert Paxton, organized a company and fought with General Jackson at New Orleans in 1814. His father, Colonel William Casey Paxton, also a native of Kentucky, commanded a company of volunteers in the Mexican War and served in the State Legislature. He had his family planning in a new home west, moving his family successively through the new territories, but staying always in that border region that gave such impetus to western American development. In 1870 James Paxton moved his family to Savoy to take a leading part in the development of Grayson County, settling in Savoy, where he bought land in cultivation, became a fine stock breeder, and acquired cattle, fine stock and acquired cattle, fine stock and fine stock.

James Paxton, the fifteenth children of William Casey and Mary Paxton, was born November 18, 1833, to William Casey and Mary Paxton. He was raised to a young man in Rochester, Missouri, in Boone County. He was graduated from the school at Rochester, and in 1854 he accompanied his father to Texas, where he bought land in cultivation, became a fine stock breeder, and acquired cattle, fine stock and fine stock.
